description: Toronto is Canada's largest city, famous for the CN Tower, its museums, and the islands along Lake Ontario.
From the historic Distillery District to Kensington Market, Toronto is one of the most multicultural cities on Earth.
Mountains meet the ocean in Vancouver, a city of beaches, ski slopes, and one of the largest urban parks in North America.
A blend of European charm and North American energy, famous for Old Montreal, poutine, and its summer festivals.
The City of Light, home to the Eiffel Tower, the Louvre, and some of the world's best cafés and bakeries.
Stroll the Seine, explore Montmartre, and discover why every visit to Paris feels like stepping into a painting.
France's gastronomic capital, where traditional bouchons, Renaissance old town, and silk-weaving history meet.
The oldest city in France, a Mediterranean port with a legendary fish market, calanques, and bouillabaisse.
A striking mix of ultramodern neighborhoods, ancient temples, and incredible food on every corner.
From the neon lights of Shibuya Crossing to the quiet gardens of the Imperial Palace, Tokyo never runs out of surprises.
Japan's ancient capital, with thousands of shrines and temples, geisha districts, and cherry blossom lined canals.
Japan's kitchen: street food paradise in Dotonbori, a spectacular castle, and the friendliest nightlife in the country.
Iconic harbour city known for the Opera House, Bondi Beach, and its sunny outdoor lifestyle.
Australia's culture capital of laneway cafés, street art, and the Great Ocean Road starting at its doorstep.
Between Table Mountain and the Atlantic Ocean, a scenic city with penguins, vineyards, and rich history.
South Africa's beating heart of gold rush history, vibrant townships, and a rising art and food scene.
The city that never sleeps: Times Square, Central Park, and a skyline recognized around the world.
Five boroughs, eight million stories: world-class museums, Broadway, and the best pizza slice of your life at 2 a.m.
Golden Gate fog, historic cable cars, and steep streets rolling down to the bay.
Art deco beaches, Cuban coffee in Little Havana, and a nightlife scene that runs until sunrise.
Beaches, samba, and Christ the Redeemer overlooking one of the most beautiful bays on Earth.
South America's largest city, a jungle of skyscrapers with an unmatched restaurant and street art scene.
Benin's vibrant economic hub, gateway to Ganvié, the stilt village on Lake Nokoué.
The official capital of Benin, with the Da Silva Museum, the Grand Mosque, and a rich Afro-Brazilian heritage.
The historic port of the slave route, home to the Door of No Return and the sacred Python Temple.
The Eternal City: the Colosseum, the Vatican, and trattorias serving pasta perfected over centuries.
A city built on water, where gondolas glide down canals and every corner hides a bridge or a bacaro.
The cradle of the Renaissance, with the Duomo, the Uffizi Gallery, and Tuscan steak in the Oltrarno.
Golden temples, floating markets, and street food that makes the city a favorite for travelers.
The rose of the north: mountain temples, night bazaars, and ethical elephant sanctuaries.
